title: Define L40S hardware tuning profile + constraints; run baseline benchmark matrix
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Ship initial L40S profile defaults (safe + stable) as part of the v1 profile pack.
- Document L40S-specific constraints (memory headroom, fragmentation risk, batching/concurrency caps) and expected behavior deltas vs H100.
- Run baseline benchmark matrix on L40S and publish results tagged by profile_version.

Scope
- Per-SKU profile definition: scheduler knobs, batching limits, prefill/decode prioritization, KV cache headroom/allocator thresholds.
- Compatibility notes: L40S instance types, driver/CUDA baseline assumptions (as enforced by schema validation), known variance across regions.
- Baseline benchmark run (matrix subset) in benchmark-lab with artifact links.

Non-goals
- Micro-optimizing kernels for L40S beyond picking safe runtime variants (kernel work tracked separately under kernel tuning).

Owners / reviewers
- Owner: Lena Fischer (batching/backpressure)
- Reviewers: Sofia Ivanova (scheduler), Omar El-Sayed (KV cache/telemetry), Irene Choi (fleet constraints), Sean Gallagher (rollout guardrails)

Deliverables
- L40S profile entry in profile pack config (with comments and rationale).
- Baseline benchmark results + summary table (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, memory/fragmentation signals).
- Inputs for Confluence page: expected-behavior-l40s + troubleshooting.

Acceptance criteria
- L40S profile passes schema validation + compatibility gates.
- No OOMs on baseline matrix at recommended concurrency caps.
- p99 latency does not regress >10% vs current production baseline for the representative mixed workload bucket (within noise bounds).
- Observability: profile_id and sku tags visible on key latency histograms; queue_ms visible for analysis.

Links
- Draft config + notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/profile-pack-config-draft.json
- Benchmark results (Jan 2026): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/l40s-results-jan-2026.json
- Benchmark matrix v1: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/benchmarks-matrix-v1.json
- Related PRs:
  - PR #24873 (loader + initial H100/L40S defs)
  - PR #24918 (L40S: cap default concurrency + preemption/backpressure)
  - PR #25071 (follow-up: adjust L40S KV cache headroom to reduce OOM risk)

Notes
L40S is more sensitive to bursty concurrency + long-tail prompt distributions. Primary failure mode we need to avoid is allocator fragmentation leading to intermittent OOM under sustained mixed prefill/decode. Defaults should bias toward stability even if that leaves some throughput on the table relative to aggressive batching.
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Spinning out L40S profile work as a standalone ticket so we can track stability outcomes independently from H100 tuning. Please ensure defaults are conservative; SRE has requested explicit headroom guardrails for L40S pools after recent OOM reports.

2026-01-13 (Lena Fischer): Proposed initial L40S constraints:
- Default concurrency cap lower than H100 (avoid deep queues under mixed workloads)
- More conservative continuous batching target (cap max_batch_tokens; avoid high variance)
- Prefer prefill fairness over decode favoritism to avoid queue buildup
Drafted knobs in profile-pack-config-draft.json; syncing with Sofia + Omar on queue policy + KV headroom.

2026-01-16 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler feedback: L40S needs stricter queue limits than H100, otherwise p99 spikes when long-prefill requests arrive behind high-throughput decode streams. Suggest enabling workload buckets (short/med/long prefill) with explicit admission control thresholds per bucket, and setting a lower max_inflight_prefill for L40S.

2026-01-17 (Omar El-Sayed): KV cache/allocator feedback: set larger safety margin for L40S to tolerate fragmentation. Recommend:
- higher reserve fraction for non-KV allocations
- earlier compaction trigger threshold
- export fragmentation_estimate + compaction_time_ms by profile_id so we can validate this change in bench + canary.
Will follow up with a small PR if we don’t already have the counters on the branch.

2026-01-20 (Irene Choi): Fleet note: L40S pools are currently heterogeneous on driver minor version across two regions. Please do not rely on “latest only” behavior; ensure profile compatibility gate allows the supported baseline and logs a clear warning when outside recommended. We can tighten once Infra standardizes.

2026-01-23 (Lena Fischer): Baseline benchmark run kicked off in benchmark-lab (matrix subset for L40S):
- Models: llama-3.1-8b-instruct, mistral-7b-instruct (representative)
- Workload buckets: short prompt/short decode; medium/medium; mixed tail (long prefill + short decode)
- Concurrency sweep: 4/8/12/16
Early results: throughput scales until ~12, then p99 climbs sharply on mixed tail. OOM observed once at concurrency=16 with long-prefill bucket; rerunning to confirm noise vs real fragmentation issue. Raw artifacts in l40s-results-jan-2026.json.

2026-01-24 (Sean Gallagher): From rollout safety perspective, please ensure the profile sets an explicit hard cap so a config drift can’t push L40S beyond the validated concurrency. Also: add a clear “rollback knob” note in the profile rationale (what to reduce first: concurrency cap vs batch target).

2026-01-27 (Lena Fischer): Rerun confirmed intermittent OOM at high concurrency is real and correlates with rising fragmentation_estimate. Adjusted defaults:
- Reduce default concurrency cap (validated stable)
- Increase KV headroom reserve and lower compaction trigger threshold
- Add backpressure earlier under mixed tail bucket
Changes landed via PR #24918 + follow-up PR #25071 (KV headroom). Re-ran baseline: no OOMs on recommended cap, p99 within acceptance threshold; p95 improved slightly due to reduced queueing.

2026-02-01 (Allison Grant): Confirmed we can slice latency histograms by profile_id + sku for the L40S runs. Queueing metric scheduler_queue_ms is present and shows expected reduction after cap + backpressure changes. Please make sure the profile references these metrics so on-call knows what to look at.

2026-02-02 (Talia Benson): Marking done. Next: feed summary into Confluence expected behavior page and add explicit “known unsafe” combinations (high concurrency + long prefill) to troubleshooting. Follow-ups should reference SUP-21958 (L40S intermittent OOM under burst) for context.
